title: What AI tools can make animated sprites or animations for static images that are not Pixel Art?
author: Cristazio
selftext: Like the title says. This is more a thing out of curiosity than for any specific projects. I know of Retro Diffusion and Pixel Lab for pixel art and I think both are already the top tools for pixel art specifically, but I have never seen tool to create sprites/animations for non-pixel art assets that is actually "good". So I was wondering if there were actual tools that were actually good for making sprites with non-pixel art characters.

replies.author: Officialedmart
replies.body:
Sure. I might be able to help you out. I’ll give you my method for removing backgrounds. Make sure your initial image has a pure white or black background and use this plugin on  Paint.Net - https://forums.getpaint.net/topic/112400-kill-color-keeper-v-12/ . 

It lets you set the targeted RBG value (in this instance, white or black) to target and change into transparency. The tolerance slider is very helpful because adjusting it lets you stay in full control over the erasing so nothing important is removed. 



Another easy method is the “Photoroom” app on IOS if you have an iphone or ipad. Not a shill, its just a really nice app. It has the functions to remove backgrounds automatically (and a brush to correct any potential errors after). It also has a smart healing brush (for touching up) and a smart object removal brush. It even has smart resizing / aspect ratio conversions. Also a bunch of other stuff like upscaling , its a robust app.. including a bunch of weird generative AI stuff but i can’t speak on the quality there i only use it to edit my stuff.

comments.author: macuseri686
comments.body:
Using a normal AI model like Nano Banana wont work for assets such as spritesheets, because AI models cant output transparency, and image models alone have no understanding of animation.

That gap is actually why I built GameLab Studio (https://gamelabstudio.co). It’s designed for game assets and it’ll generate consistent sprites, animations and full transparent bg spritesheets for anything, not just pixel art.

Gamelabs Studio MCP plugs right into your agent like Cursor, to enable rapid iteration right in your code editor

https://gamelabstudio.co/blog/mcp-setup-guide

It also enforces consistency across scale, palette, and angles, by using already generated angles of the same asset for reference, so you don’t end up with “AI asset soup” during prototyping.

We also have a seamless tileable edge-aware texture generation model

comments.author: AliAlHamwi
comments.body:
the framerate inconsistency has a real fix, and it works with any video-to-frames pipeline: stop extracting every frame. Pick a target fps up front, say 10 or 12, and pull frames at that rate with ffmpeg using -vf fps=12. Every clip then lands on identical timing no matter what the video model decided internally. For the background problem, rembg will batch a whole folder and it handles the messy interior edges that flat black or white keying misses, which is the part you said you were stuck removing by hand.

that said, you are right that the whole pipeline is a lot of ceremony for one animation. Retro Diffusion and PixelLab are the correct picks for pixel art, no argument there. For non-pixel, the one I would point you at is Ludo.ai: it generates sprite animations in 30+ styles, pixel and non-pixel both, and the output is a transparent PNG spritesheet or individual frames directly, so the extraction and background removal steps are gone. There is also an option to get the sheet as it was before background removal, so if the automatic cutout eats something it should not have, you fix it from the original instead of regenerating. Conflict of interest flag: my own work goes into Ludo, so verify that claim yourself rather than taking my word for it. The video route still has a place if you are chasing the specific look of a specific video model, just go in knowing you will be doing the cleanup you already described.
